items.item_text: Preferred RN or another clinical certification
Preferred Certified risk adjustment coder certification.
Professional certifications in Program Management, Change Management, Lean, Six Sigma, Agile, Healthcare Operations, Healthcare Technology, or related disciplines are preferred.
Bachelors degree in healthcare administration, Health Policy, Business Administration, or a related field is required.
Advanced degree preferred (MBA, MHA, MPH, MS, or equivalent graduate degree) preferred

Minimum eight (8) years of progressive leadership experience within healthcare, including health plans, integrated delivery systems, healthcare operations, population health, revenue cycle, risk adjustment, care delivery transformation, healthcare technology, consulting, or related disciplines.
Preferred three (3) years of healthcare consulting experience supporting large-scale strategic, operational, technology, or organizational transformation initiatives.

Requires significant direct risk adjustment experience with demonstrated understanding of prospective and retrospective risk adjustment programs, documentation and coding operations, encounter data, value-based reimbursement methodologies, revenue capture processes, and regulatory requirements.
Experience may be obtained through a nationally recognized consulting firm or internal consulting/transformation organization.
Experience creating and executing enterprise implementation roadmaps, governance structures, accountability frameworks, operating models, and organizational change strategies.

Experience partnering with physician leaders, operational leaders, finance organizations, technology organizations, and executive leadership teams to drive business outcomes and large-scale adoption of new capabilities.
Experience developing executive-level presentations, business cases, strategic recommendations, implementation plans, and performance reporting for senior leaders and governing bodies.
Experience leading highly matrixed organizations and driving results through influence rather than direct authority.

Strategy and Transformation Leadership: Lead the overall strategy, governance, operating model, implementation roadmap, and execution of the CDVCUE initiative. Establish enterprise objectives, key milestones, success metrics, accountability frameworks, and organizational priorities. Ensure initiative activities remain aligned with enterprise strategy, value-based care objectives, regulatory requirements, and financial performance goals.

Cross-Functional Leadership and Organizational Alignment: Develop strong working relationships with executive leaders across National Health Plan, Permanente Medical Groups, Care Delivery, Technology, Revenue Cycle, Claims, Finance, Compliance, Legal, Consumer Experience, Scheduling, and Benefits Administration. Create alignment on priorities, establish shared ownership of outcomes, and facilitate resolution of cross-functional issues and competing priorities.

Implementation and Program Execution: Translate strategic objectives into executable implementation plans with defined workstreams, deliverables, dependencies, timelines, and resource requirements. Monitor progress, manage risks, escalate barriers, and ensure timely achievement of critical milestones. Drive accountability for execution across matrixed teams and stakeholders.

Full Kit Solution Development and Operational Integration: Oversee the design, development, testing, implementation, and operational integration of Clinical Full Kit, Scheduling Full Kit, Patient Encounter, and Submission Full Kit capabilities. Ensure solutions are scalable, sustainable, standardized where appropriate, and integrated across workflows, technologies, and organizational boundaries.

Financial and Business Value Realization: Work closely with Finance, Risk Adjustment, Revenue Cycle, and business leaders to establish value realization targets and benefit tracking methodologies. Monitor achievement of operational, clinical, and financial outcomes and ensure initiatives support reimbursement integrity, margin improvement, affordability goals, and responsible stewardship of resources.

Technology Enablement and Process Transformation: Partner with technology and operational leaders to identify opportunities for automation, workflow optimization, analytics, decision support tools, artificial intelligence capabilities, data quality improvements, and process redesign. Ensure technology investments enable sustainable improvements in care delivery, documentation, coding, encounter management, and data submission processes.

Compliance, Risk Management, and Governance: Partner with Legal, Compliance, Privacy, Internal Audit, and operational leaders to identify risks, implement controls, maintain regulatory compliance, and ensure initiative activities align with Kaiser Permanente policies, standards, and ethical expectations.
Demonstrated success leading enterprise-wide transformation initiatives requiring coordination across multiple business units, markets, regions, executive stakeholders, and operational teams.
Knowledge of integrated healthcare delivery systems, payer-provider models, and value-based care arrangements strongly preferred.
